thread.title: Trade war is still the biggest ‘tail risk,’ say global fund managers - MarketWatch

author: William Watts
title: Trade war is still the biggest ‘tail risk,’ say global fund managers - MarketWatch
text:
Deputy markets editor
Global fund managers still see a trade war as the biggest “tail risk” facing investors.
Around 57% of fund managers cited “trade war” as the biggest tail risk, putting it at the top of the list for a third straight month, the Bank of America Merrill Lynch survey of fund managers found. The survey of 185 managers with $534 billion in assets under management was conducted between Aug. 3 and 9.
Trade-war tracker: Here are the levies imposed and threatened
Meanwhile, investors have continued to pile into U.S. stocks. The survey found participants were the most overweight U.S. equities since January 2015. Allocation to U.S. equities rose 10 percentage point to a net 19% overweight, making it the top equity region for the first time in five years. The earnings outlook for U.S. companies was at a 17-year high.
The S&P 500 SPX, -0.40% exited correction territory in July and remains less than 2% below its all-time high set in January.
At the same time, the survey found the average cash level rose to 5% from 4.7%. According to BAML, a reading above 4.5% is a contrarian “buy” signal.
The survey, which wrapped up before Turkey’s currency crisis hit critical mass, found investors were slightly underweight emerging market equities.
Related : Why Turkey’s crisis is rattling European bank stocks and the euro
In terms of rotation, the survey showed participants are buying banks KBWB, -1.10% and continue to flock to perceived havens like U.S. equities and cash, while selling commodity sectors and defensive sectors and regions like materials, energy and U.K. equities UKX, -0.20% , BAML said.
Allocation to tech inched down a percentage point to net 32% overweight, still leaving it the most favored sector.
The survey found that the “long FAANG+BAT” position was identified as the “most crowded” trade for the seventh straight month. The double acronym refers to U.S. tech giants Facebook Inc. FB, -0.12% Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.65% Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, +0.52% Netflix Inc. NFLX, -1.32% and Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOG, -0.21% GOOGL, -0.31% combined with Chinese tech juggernauts Baidu Inc. BIDU, -1.15% Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. BABA, -1.29% and Tencent Holdings Ltd. 0700, -3.43%
Cited by 54% of respondents, the trade is the most crowded outright since long dollar in December 2015, the survey found. William Watts William Watts is MarketWatch's deputy markets editor, based in New York. Follow him on Twitter @wlwatts. We Want to Hear from You
